title: The Atmosphere and Climate
seo_title: Year 8 Science: The Atmosphere and Climate Worksheets (Carbon Cycle, Greenhouse Effect)
standard_text: The composition of the atmosphere; the production of carbon dioxide by human activity and the impact on climate; the carbon cycle.
meta_desc: Free Year 8 science worksheets on the atmosphere and climate: the gases in air, the carbon cycle, fossil fuels, the greenhouse effect, carbon dioxide data and climate change. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: Carbon dioxide traps heat in the atmosphere.
key_sub: Air is 78% nitrogen and 21% oxygen; burning fossil fuels adds carbon dioxide.
body_html:
How to think about it

The atmosphere is mostly nitrogen and oxygen, with a little carbon dioxide.

  • Air: about 78% nitrogen, 21% oxygen, 1% argon, 0.04% carbon dioxide.
  • Carbon cycle: photosynthesis removes carbon dioxide; respiration, decay and burning add it.
  • Greenhouse gases trap heat. Burning fossil fuels has raised carbon dioxide and warmed the climate.
Example

Burning coal: what does it add to the air?

Coal is mostly carbon

Answer: carbon dioxide

Example

Planting forests: effect on carbon dioxide?

Photosynthesis

Answer: removes it

Common mistakes

  • Thinking the air is mostly oxygen.
  • Blaming the greenhouse effect on the ozone hole.
  • Mixing up weather and climate.

faq.q: What is the air made of?
faq.a: About 78% nitrogen, 21% oxygen, just under 1% argon and about 0.04% carbon dioxide, with some water vapour.
The way carbon moves between the air, living things, oceans and rocks. Photosynthesis removes carbon dioxide; respiration, decay and combustion return it.
Burning fossil fuels and cutting down forests have increased carbon dioxide and other greenhouse gases, which trap more heat.
